clue.text: Bars the irrigation of parts of the course

definitions.meaning: pubs or bars where people go to drink

definitions.text: the irrigation of parts of the course
definitions.meaning: a playful reading: sprinkling water on the holes of a golf course

explanation.surface: A groundsman describes how parts of the golf course get irrigated.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking haunts are jokingly called watering holes, and a golf course's holes may literally be watered.

clue.text: The gallery adore them, but they don't last long

definitions.text: The gallery adore them, but they don't last long

parts.words: The gallery adore them, but they don't last long
parts.note: the top gallery of a theatre is called 'the gods', so the people the gallery adores are those loved by the gods, who in the proverb die young

explanation.surface: Theatre favourites with the cheap seats never have long careers.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'those whom the gods love die young'; 'the gods' is the slang name for the highest, cheapest gallery in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase for people who die young, because the deities cherish them and take them early.

clue.text: Unit provided by the amphibious troops

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines, Britain's sea-and-land infantry

explanation.surface: A military unit is supplied by the marines.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in Britain for billing gas.

clue.text: Disorderly behaviour in queues grabbing eats

indicators.note: the first piece seizes the second, holding it inside

parts.note: queues are lines or rows of people
to eat a meal is to dine; he eats = he dines

explanation.surface: Unruly conduct in lines of people where someone snatches food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiness is noisy, disorderly conduct.

clue.text: Ignore marked slight

definitions.meaning: as a verb: fail to attend to
as a noun: a pointed failure to pay attention, a snub

explanation.surface: Disregard a noticeably small insult.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect is to disregard; as a noun it is a conspicuous lack of attention, a kind of snub.

clue.text: Women under house arrest?

parts.note: a jokey description of the wives and concubines kept secluded in a sultan's household

explanation.surface: Women confined to their home by the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the secluded women's quarters of a Muslim household, and the women kept there.

clue.text: Nothing perfunctory may be seen as a sign of affection

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
a token gesture is a perfunctory one, made for form's sake

explanation.surface: Doing nothing but going through the motions might pass for fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: A love token is a small gift given as a sign of affection.

clue.text: Ambiguous, advice to Mediterranean tourists

parts.note: the old saying urges travellers to visit the Italian city before death, which can also be read as a recommendation to visit it and then die

explanation.surface: A guidebook's recommendation to travellers in southern Europe can be read two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means the Italian port is so beautiful you can die content once you have seen it.

clue.text: How dry the wine sounds!

indicators.note: the clue says the word for the wine is heard, giving a spelling that sounds like it

parts.note: Beaune is a Burgundy wine, named after its town

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how dry a wine sounds when described.
explanation.walkthrough: Something extremely dry is 'bone dry', so the word answers 'how dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone is the intensifier in 'bone dry', saying just how dry something is.

clue.text: Carry on with romancing initiated in punt

parts.note: to carry on a war is to wage it

indicators.note: romancing is started, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Continuing a courtship that began on a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like a boat on the river; here it is the British slang for a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a bet, the same as a wager.

clue.text: Compete with Panorama

parts.note: to compete is to vie

explanation.surface: Competing against the BBC current-affairs programme Panorama.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC current-affairs programme, hence the italics; here it is just a wide prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide view.

clue.text: Poisoning, for instance, one maiden too many in mad pantomime

indicators.note: the fodder holds a letter beyond what is needed, which is set aside
mad signals that the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: M is one maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A frantic Christmas pantomime has one too many young women and poisons someone.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTOMIME has two Ms; 'one maiden too many' removes one, and 'mad' rearranges the other eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaine is a substance once blamed for food poisoning, as in 'ptomaine poisoning'.

clue.text: Common substitute for umlaut

indicators.note: the letters of umlaut are swapped around to stand in its place

explanation.surface: A frequent replacement for the two dots over a German vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutual is shared or held in common.

clue.text: Unresponsive landlord's rule no longer observed

parts.note: something unresponsive is dead
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A landlord who ignores tenants has a regulation that nobody follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead letter is a law still on the books but no longer enforced.

clue.text: Putting on ice made half of it effervesce

indicators.note: the second half of the word made is taken

parts.note: to ferment is to bubble or effervesce

explanation.surface: Chilling a drink made half of it fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on ice' means postponing, not chilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something on ice is postponing it, which is deferment.

clue.text: Replace ' assistant without offence when promoted

indicators.note: in a down answer, promotion raises the letters so they read from bottom to top
without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: an assistant is a helper
an offence against God is a sin

explanation.surface: Substitute an aide who has committed no offence when giving promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'when promoted' in a down clue raises the whole build so it reads from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill up again, replacing what was used.

clue.text: Finish off the crustaceans right away

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is removed

parts.note: krill are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans

explanation.surface: Finishing off the shellfish at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately' but splits into R and the removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to kill an animal or opponent is to finish it off for good.

clue.text: Perform very loudly in shed

parts.note: to perform a task is to do it
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Doing a loud show in a garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is the verb: take off.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff a hat or garment is to take it off, to shed it.

clue.text: Spineless English collapsing into torpor

indicators.note: collapsing breaks the letters down into a new order

explanation.surface: Weak-willed Englishmen falling into a sluggish state.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is sluggish drowsiness, close to sleepiness.

clue.text: Make a count, perhaps, and be left with none going astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Do some arithmetic and find nothing left after it goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a count' looks like adding up, but count is the noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the peerage, for example as a count.

clue.text: Liveliness when fairy's finale starts

indicators.note: the last letter of the fairy word goes to the front

parts.note: a sprite is a fairy or elf

explanation.surface: Spirited energy as the fairy's grand last act begins.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRITE with its final E moved to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit and spirit.

clue.text: Island covered with sailors' bones

parts.note: tars are sailors

explanation.surface: An island overrun by the skeletons of sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle and foot.

clue.text: It's annoying to be wanting about a pound

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: wanting something is needing it
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: It is irritating to be short of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means provoking or irritating someone.

clue.text: Purchase from bar giving rise to celebration

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters rise, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a revel is a celebration

explanation.surface: Buying drinks at a pub sparks a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but it is the mechanical grip a bar gives when used to prise something.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar used to get purchase, or leverage, on a load.

clue.text: Solid figure standing in middle of motorway

definitions.meaning: a three-dimensional shape with a round base and a point
the plastic markers placed on roads during roadworks

explanation.surface: A statue stands in the centre of a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a geometric solid and also a traffic marker set out on roads.

clue.text: Teacher of law has to talk endlessly

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for talk is cut off

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length

explanation.surface: A law lecturer has to chatter without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher of religious law.

clue.text: Consult the Recorder — nothing's missing

indicators.note: missing means the letter for nothing is dropped

parts.note: a video is a recorder of TV programmes
O is nothing, the figure zero

explanation.surface: Ask the court recorder, and find nothing has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a judge or a flute; here it is a video recorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Vide, Latin for 'see', directs a reader to consult another passage.

clue.text: Stuff — as at an Arab feast?

definitions.meaning: to stuff oneself, gorge on food
a joke reading: an Arab is a breed of horse, so its feast is eating as a horse does

explanation.surface: Gorging oneself at a lavish Middle Eastern banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat like a horse is to eat a great deal, to stuff oneself.
